evidence: Type census of the frozen task: gates 3 binary (render/judge.toml:20; constraints/judge.toml:20,29), functional 40 binary (functional/judge.toml, every [[criterion]] has type = "binary", lines 26-377), polish 6 binary (polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56,65), visual 3 likert with points = 5 (visual/judge.toml:20-21, 36-37, 52-53). No other type appears. Likert anchors: each of the three visual criteria describes every level 5,4,3,2,1,0 on its own line (visual/judge.toml:25-30, 41-46, 57-62), matching the 0-5 shape of the frozen template visual dimension (template visual/judge.toml:25-33), and visual/prompt.md:7 tells the judge 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 using the anchors written in it; 0 is used only when the thing being judged is not shown at all', consistent with the gate-fail instruction at prompt.md:5. The three likert criteria grade degree-of-quality only (editor readability, workspace arrangement, component finish) and each excludes the binary behaviours graded elsewhere ('not whether token categories are correct', visual/judge.toml:24; prompt.md:19). Binary criteria checked for hidden craft: every functional and polish description states one conjunctive bar and closes with explicit 'Fails if ...' conditions on observable facts (e.g. polish/judge.toml:23 focus reachable and visible; :68 no sideways scroll, five areas reachable, typing and Run work at 390 px; functional/judge.toml:173 five visibly different treatments, 'No fixed colour values are required'). The softest wording is 'understandable visible names' (polish/judge.toml:32) but its fail condition is the observable 'a main control has no readable name', and the template polish dimension is likewise all binary (template polish/judge.toml:20,30,41,52). So no craft criterion is binary and no likert block lacks an anchor, which are the two defects the skill says to flag (SKILL.md:65; quality-checks.md:169-170). Presence of likert is not a finding despite the workbook internal annotation. Adversarial reading: a broken app with misaligned line numbers still earns partial visual credit (anchor 2) rather than a cliff, which is the intended gradation; a conforming plain but tidy app is not forced to 0 because 0 is reserved for 'not shown'. Non-blocking observation (P3, belongs to rows 33/48 rather than this one): visual/prompt.md:20 says 'Do not penalize the palette chosen by the app' while visual/judge.toml:56-57 grades 'colour harmony' and 'one palette'; these reconcile as choice-of-palette versus internal consistency, but one clarifying clause would remove the second reading. Not measured: no configured judge run exists for the visual dimension (raw-evidence-index.json limitations: 'Visual ratings ... are not measured'), so whether the judge actually returns well-spread 0-5 values is unobserved; this row is a static type/anchor fit check and passes on the shipped text.
